title: Pivot Engine Automatically Queues Follow-Up Scans from Confirmed Findings
goal: When the pivot engine detects an access-confirming finding (XSS, SQLi, SSRF, RCE, path traversal, auth bypass), it currently creates a TargetContextDocument recording the pivot vantage — but it does NOT queue any follow-up task. This task wires the pivot engine into the ai_loop run path so that: (1) for ai_loop runs, after a pivot context doc is created, a follow-up passive task is automatically queued using the pivot context's recommended_tools and target; (2) for standard/chain runs, the pivot doc is created as before (review-gated proposal only). The follow-up task must be a registered runner within scope, dispatched through the existing task_dispatch path. Example chain: httpx finds XSS → pivot engine creates ssrf_outbound_pivot context → queues auth-flow task against the target with the XSS parameter as context → auth-flow finds authenticated endpoint → pivot engine creates session_token_pivot context → queues idor-bac task.
generation_reason: generate_pivot_contexts_for_run() creates context documents but does not queue tasks. The pivot chain only advances if the operator manually approves proposals. For ai_loop runs this must be automatic.

constraints.active_task_gate: Do not implement until this package is the single active task in NEXT_TASK.md.
constraints.ai_loop_only: Automatic pivot task dispatch only applies to runs where run_uses_ai_loop(run) is True. Standard and chain runs get proposals only.
constraints.registered_runners_only: Only dispatch tasks for tools in the registered runner registry. Do not invent new runner names.
constraints.passive_first: Only auto-dispatch the first follow-up tool from the pivot context recommended_tools if it is passive tier. Active tools require operator approval.
constraints.scope_boundary: The follow-up task target must pass validate_target_is_allowed(scope, target) before dispatch.
constraints.idempotent: Already-queued pivot follow-ups must not be re-queued on repeat calls.
constraints.scope_creep_guard: Keep implementation bounded to this task package. Defer broader scanner, exploit-chain, UI, or runtime work to separately queued packages.

implementation_notes.where: In _maybe_detect_and_record_pivots() in tasks.py, after generate_pivot_contexts_for_run() returns created docs, for each doc check if the run uses ai_loop and the first recommended tool is passive tier. If so, create a Task for that tool targeting the pivot endpoint and dispatch it.
implementation_notes.task_creation: Use the same pattern as _queue_passive_loop_task() in assessment_loop.py to create the Task record and link it to the pivot context document.
implementation_notes.deduplication: Store the queued task id in the pivot context doc's provenance_json under 'follow_up_task_id'. Skip if already set.

acceptance_criteria: For an ai_loop run, when an SSRF finding is confirmed, a follow-up httpx task is automatically queued targeting the SSRF endpoint.
For a standard run, only a proposal is created — no automatic dispatch.
The queued task id is stored in the pivot context document's provenance_json.
Running pivot detection twice does not create duplicate tasks.

out_of_scope: Running live public target scans without explicit operator authorization and approved scope.
Bypassing approval gates, scope/ROE boundaries, runtime binding, credential protections, or kill-switch behavior.
Materializing credentials or sensitive data outside protected references.
